title: Gratitude for the scholars

segments.voice: Yesterday, what you still ask, and your line: keep asking. Did you write your question down, or ask someone who knows more? Hold on to whoever answered. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-three.

Every answer this year had someone standing behind it. The chain of a hadith: a row of names, each one checked. The rule for praying while traveling: a jurist who weighed the reports, and a student who copied his notes, and a teacher who explained them to the next student. Some of them you will never hear of. They sat with questions like the one you kept yesterday, and they wrote down what they found and what they weren't sure of. Today is a thank-you. Centuries of careful people, and why their care mattered.
screen: `EVERY ANSWER HAS SOMEONE BEHIND IT.` → `NAMES YOU'LL NEVER HEAR.` → `CENTURIES OF CAREFUL PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: First, someone has to stay and learn. The Qur'an says, in paraphrase, that the believers should not all go out at once: from every group, a party should stay behind to gain understanding of the religion, and teach their people when they come back. Learning is named as a job worth staying home for. Second, what the scholars inherit. In a hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase, that the scholars are the heirs of the prophets. The prophets left no gold and no silver. They left knowledge, and whoever takes it takes a large share. Third, why they were careful. The Qur'an counts among forbidden things, in paraphrase, saying about Allah what you do not know. So the scholars this year met, from Abu Hanifa and Malik to Ja'far al-Sadiq to Karimah al-Marwaziyyah teaching Bukhari's collection, were not careful because they were fussy. Speaking for God without knowledge was a serious wrong to them. That is why they checked chains, argued over a single word, and wrote down where they disagreed. Fourth, what the teacher receives. In a hadith in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says, in paraphrase, that Allah and His angels, and the people of the heavens and the earth, even the ant in its hole and even the fish, send blessings on the one who teaches people good. So the hadith itself sends blessing after the teacher, from the ant in its hole to the angels. The scholars were careful, and the texts ask that their care be remembered.
screen: `A PARTY STAYS BEHIND TO LEARN.` · `HEIRS OF THE PROPHETS.` · `CAREFUL, BECAUSE IT WAS SERIOUS.` · `EVEN THE ANT AND THE FISH.`

segments.voice: The practice: pray for them. Settle into the sit, and breathe. Bring back one scholar from this year, a name you remember: a jurist, a collector of hadith, a woman who taught. If you pray, you can say after their name the words Muslims use for those who have died: rahimahullah, may Allah have mercy on him, or rahimahallah for a woman. If you don't pray, simply hold the name, and thank that person quietly for the care they took. Then let the name go, and rest in the breath. The bell holds the time.
Gratitude for the scholars. Thanks for the people who stayed behind to learn, checked every link, and feared saying about God what they did not know. Today's word.

Your line: they were careful. Today, before you say something about your faith or anyone else's, take one extra second to check that you actually know it. Tomorrow, gratitude for the ordinary. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims say rahimahullah, may Allah have mercy on him, after the name of a scholar who has died, and teachers often open a lesson by naming the scholars whose books they are teaching from.
